doc.title: Buddy Collette interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999

chapter: Studio work and Stars of Swing
title: The Joe Swanson band and arranger Paul Villipeig
summary: He recalls a band led by Joe Swanson with a patron's money and a gifted arranger.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Gee. I wonder if that music is still around? Do you think it still exists?

I don’t know. We did some great stuff in those days with a band called Joe Swanson, he was the leader. Joe Swanson couldn’t play very well though. There was a lady there with © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-
quite a bit of money that wanted him to have a band. And he had a guy named Paul Villipeig, do you know that name?

Oh he was a great arranger. I think he committed suicide later. But I mean who knows what his other problems were, but he could sure write. And he wrote for that band and we had, I know I was there, John Ewing the trombone player and I don’t think Lucky was there, maybe Teddy Edwards or somebody, but what a band. And then Mingus did some early stuff too for I don’t know what record was it — I’ve got the tape at home by the way, I should remember it.
